purpose: Profile the current durable QoS 2 serial throughput gap (21,292 vs 29,146/s, 0.731x Mosquitto).

capture.host_load_note: The shared host also ran unrelated jobs; absolute throughput is lower than the matrix median, but the zero-loss symbol ranking is stable.

conclusions: Durable serial QoS 2 is dominated by the same zio runtime wait/executor/loop/clock costs seen in transient serial QoS 2: clock_gettime alone is 12.58% self and the loop/executor/waiter stack accounts for roughly half the sampled cycles.

Protocol-side costs are distributed across handlePubRel (22.04% children), the durable session packet drain/write path (writePreparedSessionTransmission 5.78%, writeSessionPublish 3.90%, drainOne 1.92%) and the delivery flush path (11.72% children).

No single cheap protocol hotspot explains the 0.731x durable serial gap. Closing it requires reducing per-message runtime wakeups/clock reads or restructuring the durable session packet path, not a local micro-optimization.
The earlier queue-batching experiment and transient session-drain skip both failed for related reasons; future work must leave the QoS 2/session path structurally intact.
